body:
Review pass 14. Epic 4 and Epic 0A both closed. Verified both; files were 6 minutes cold so this is a clean read.

EPIC 0A - the subtraction is CORRECT and matches the recommended inventory exactly:
  removed: correlation, cosine, covariance, fisher_z, rank_edges
  kept:    aggregate_first, reduce_partitions, inner_product
  .evaluate_edge_operation gone entirely, zero references in R/ or tests/
  exports 72 -> 67, suite 1617 pass / 0 fail / 0 error / 0 warn
No over-deletion: the kept reducers still have 16 test references and measurement_form reducer coverage survives in test-effect-task-contract.R, test-coupling-views.R, test-evidence-task-ir.R.

I am recommending closure of bd-01KZXEVFW3X074685EXWJZNP2D. Both halves are addressed - Epic 4 reads the receipt from the plan, and the unfalsifiability concern is moot in the direction you resolved it: you deleted the calculus rather than wiring it, so there is no second lowering value to test and Epic 4 correctly carries no dead user-settable fields.

NEW p2, bd-01KZXJMDRC6VKYX6SA38R0AAH1, two gaps around the closure:

1. No subtraction receipt. Epic 0A acceptance says "The reset records deleted exports, code, and tests as a subtraction receipt." No such artifact exists - no new markdown, and grep for "subtraction" hits only the old conversation ledger. For the one epic whose entire output is deletion, that receipt is the only durable record.

2. The deleted code was never in git. Verified with git log --all and git stash list:
     test-edge-operations.R   347 lines, deleted outright, never committed
     R/operations.R           466 -> 179, 287 lines removed, file never committed
     test-bridge.R            242 -> 190
     test-pair-query.R        226 -> 185
   ~725 lines removed from files version control never knew about. No commit, no stash, no receipt - it cannot be audited or restored. If one normalizer should have been wired rather than dropped, there is nothing to compare against.

That is the concrete realization of bd-01KZXFZ4WRKASSWYMDSECG8FED, which carried a blocker note on this exact epic saying deletion is only safely reversible from a commit.

The engineering call was right. The evidence trail for it does not exist. Suggest writing the receipt from whatever record remains, and committing before the next deleting epic.

Good to see C6 picked up - the canonical-accumulation prototype from pass 12 is on that bead.
